findings.problem: status is pub String instead of a domain enum. Any arbitrary string value can be assigned, making invalid workflow states representable and unenforceable at the type level.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can set budget.status to any string (e.g. "deleted", "pending", ""), bypassing workflow invariants. No compiler guarantee that status is a valid lifecycle value.
findings.fix: Replace `pub status: String` with `pub status: BudgetStatus` where `BudgetStatus` is a non-exhaustive enum with explicit variants (e.g. `Validating`, `Validated`, `Sent`).

findings.problem: is_validated is a pub bool instead of an enum or typestate field. Booleans for lifecycle flags are easily left in inconsistent combinations.
findings.failure_mode: A BudgetWorkflow can exist with is_validated=false, is_sent=true, and status="sent" -- a logically impossible state where an unvalidated budget is already sent.
findings.fix: Replace `is_validated: bool` with a typed field in the status enum or a dedicated typestate parameter. The valid/invalid lifecycle should be encoded in the enum variants.

findings.problem: is_sent is a pub bool instead of an enum or typestate field. It is redundant with status="sent" and can diverge.
findings.failure_mode: is_sent=true and status="pending" can coexist, creating contradictory workflow state. The bool does not enforce that sent_at_epoch_ms is set.
findings.fix: Remove `is_sent: bool` entirely. Encode the sent state in the BudgetStatus enum and make sent_at_epoch_ms required (not Option) when the status variant is Sent.

findings.problem: All fields of BudgetWorkflow are pub, allowing external mutation of the entire struct. Data is not valid-by-construction and has no encapsulation.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can set arbitrary field combinations, creating invalid states without going through the workflow transition logic. No invariant enforcement.
findings.fix: Make fields private (or use newtype/enum wrapping) and expose only a fallible constructor and transition methods (e.g. `BudgetWorkflow::new(...)`, `.mark_sent()`) that enforce invariants.

findings.problem: mark_sent does not enforce preconditions: it does not check that the budget is validated, not already sent, or that sent_at_epoch_ms should be set.
findings.failure_mode: An unvalidated budget can be marked sent. A budget can be marked sent multiple times. sent_at_epoch_ms remains None even after being marked sent, producing contradictory state.
findings.fix: Change `mark_sent` to a fallible method on the struct that checks status is in a pre-sent state, sets sent_at_epoch_ms to the current time (via injectable clock), and transitions to a Sent variant. Signature: `fn mark_sent(self) -> Result<BudgetWorkflow, WorkflowError>`.

findings.problem: id is pub String instead of a domain newtype. Budget IDs are domain values that should have their own type with parsing/formatting guarantees.
findings.failure_mode: Any string can be used as a budget ID. Typos, empty strings, or malformed IDs are representable. No validation at the type level.
findings.fix: Replace `pub id: String` with `pub id: BudgetId` where BudgetId is a newtype with a fallible constructor that validates format (e.g. `impl BudgetId { fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self, ...> }`).

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is Option<u64> and is pub. The timestamp is a side-effect value that should not be freely set by callers.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can set sent_at_epoch_ms manually, bypassing the time-of-sent invariant. None is valid even when the budget is supposedly sent, creating data inconsistency.
findings.fix: Make sent_at_epoch_ms private. When transitioning to Sent variant, the constructor/method sets it. Consider using `u64` (non-optional) in the Sent variant since the timestamp is required when sent.

findings.problem: mark_sent uses `.to_string()` to assign a string literal to status. This creates an unnecessary heap allocation.
findings.failure_mode: Performance degradation from redundant heap allocation on every call. With `String` for status, all transitions require allocation instead of zero-copy enum variant matching.
findings.fix: Replace String with an enum so status transitions are zero-allocation variant switches. Use `self.status = BudgetStatus::Sent` instead of `.to_string()`.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or any BudgetWorkflow operation
no profiler data for allocation patterns in the workflow
no allocation audit for BudgetWorkflow lifecycle
no command-line evidence or test coverage for workflow transition invariants
residual_risk: The entire BudgetWorkflow model is built on primitive types (String, bool, Option<u64>) that make illegal states fully representable. Without enum-based status, typestates, and a closed transition API, any caller can construct contradictory workflow states. Static review only; no commands run.
